values.note: $20 a night. A Recreation Passport is required for vehicle entry to every state forest campground.

fees.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/braycreek ('Overnight fees ($20 for most sites)') + https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/things-to-do/camping-and-lodging/state-forest-campgrounds/amenity-table (Bray Creek: nightly fee $20; 'A Recreation Passport (park pass) is required for vehicle entry into all state park and forest campgrounds'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Drinking water from a hand-pump well. Carry-in access to the Baldwin River down a short set of stairs beside the day-use parking area (room for 2-3 vehicles). ORVs may be ridden from a campsite to reach the area's routes; other ORV use in the campground is prohibited.

facilities.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/braycreek ('There are vault toilets', 'Potable (drinking) water is available from a hand-pump well', 'Carry-in access is located adjacent to the day-use parking area, down a short set of stairs. The small parking area can accommodate 2-3 vehicles', 'ORV can be ridden from a campsite to access these routes. All other ORV use within the campground is prohibited'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: No reservations or advance payment. Registration is online or by phone using the number or website posted at the campground, no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of arrival; the site must then be set up and occupied. Clip the hang tag (site, due-out date, booking number) to the site post.

booking.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/braycreek ('No reservations. Sites available on a first-come, first-served basis. All registrations now processed online or via phone', 'You can register no earlier than 8 a.m. on the day of your arrival', 'we do not accept advance payments or reservations', 'Camping is limited to a 15-day maximum stay') + amenity table ('Reservable at MiDNRReservations.com': no), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Nine sites 'for tent and small trailer use' (the DNR's standard state forest wording). No length limit posted. One camping unit and six people per site.

sites.source: https://www.michigan.gov/recsearch/sfcampgroundsa-m/braycreek ('There are nine sites for tent and small trailer use', 'One camping unit and six people are allowed per site') + amenity table (9 campsites), read 2026-10-25

note: Secluded rustic Michigan DNR state forest campground on the Baldwin River at its confluence with Bray Creek, 2.3 miles northeast of Baldwin via M-37, Merriville Road and 40th Street. Trout fishing; hiking and mountain biking on the Pine Forest Pathway; ORV routes nearby (Little O/Big O 4 miles northwest). --Claude
summary: DNR page + SF amenity table: 9 tent/small-trailer sites, $20 + Recreation Passport, no electric, vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come only with same-day online/phone registration from 8 a.m. (booking.note), 15-day max (now on the entry); season open all year, roads not plowed (already manual, matches); phone 231-745-9465 (Baldwin Field Office) matches. Note trimmed of field restatements.
flags: Waterfront re-audit lead: the DNR page says the campground is 'situated along the banks of the Baldwin River' and 'The confluence of Bray Creek and the Baldwin River run adjacent to the campground'; the entry has 'not waterfront' (river access is down a set of stairs by the day-use area).
